title: A chromosome-scale genome assembly of the Swiss Lolium multiflorum ecotype Tremona reveals a scalable method to purge spurious duplications
authors: Piat, L., Herren, G., Grieder, C. et al.
abstract: Italian ryegrass (Lolium multiflorum) is a key temperate forage species underpinning livestock production in Europe. Genomic resources remain limited by its large (2.2 Gb), repetitive, and highly heterozygous genome. Here, we present a high-quality chromosome-scale genome assembly of the Swiss L. multiflorum ecotype Tremona, collected in 2008 in Ticino, Switzerland, and subsequently incorporated into recurrent breeding cycles in the Swiss breeding program.
